newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-Vickers pressed by Rolls tooling.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Vickers pressed by Rolls tooling.

text.p: A high, ongoing level of investment to gear up for production of the next Rolls-Royce luxury car is pressing on profitability, the chief executive of the marque's parent group Vickers Plc said on Thursday.

Speaking after Vickers reported what it called a "useful" set of interim results, with group pretax profit up 18 percent to 31.8 million stg, Sir Colin Chandler said investment at Rolls and at automotive engineering unit Cosworth took its toll.
"We are investing a lot at the moment...when doing that, we obviously are not getting a very good return on sales," he told Reuters in a telephone interview.
Chandler said he was confident that the business climate and state of readiness of the group's units would support continued growth through the rest of the year.

Automotive earnings are in a sensitive phase, however, because, even though sales of Rolls-Royce and Bentley cars have shown strong growth in the first half of this year, the sales mix has included fewer higher-margin "bespoke individual cars".
Going forward, Chandler said, Rolls' sales prospects would be dependent on the rate of increase of global GDP, which on current forecasts appears to be on a steady course.
"I think we'll see pretty steady growth," he said.

The heavy spend on design engineering and tooling for the new four-door Rolls-Royce and Bentley cars will continue and Chandler said the company expected it would spur along sales and allow them to break out of the expected gentle uptrend.
"What will help is the new model, because we believe there is pent-up demand. We do see some good growth," he said.
The profit margin dilution caused by the automotive division's sustained capital expenditure was also having an impact on cashflow, Chandler acknowleged.
In the six months to the end of June, Vickers slipped to being slightly geared, at 8.0 percent, from having net cash.
Chandler made clear that the announced plan for him to succeed Sir Richard Lloyd as chairman in April next year would involve the company seeking a new chief executive in time.
At first, Chandler will not drop his current job, but he said "the plan is for me to keep both jobs for about a year. During that time we will start a process to look for a new chief executive."

Chris Woodwark, currently executive director in charge of automotive, will be promoted to chief operating officer next April. Chandler said that Woodwark was obviously one candidate for consideration for the chief executive post.
